title: Phase-aware Traffic Semaphore prototype for staged rollouts with emergency brakes
creator: Ava Kim
description: Design a compact, phase-oriented UI metaphor ("traffic semaphore") for composing staged rollouts. The goal is to give operators a single visual control that communicates progress, health, and emergency intervention options across multiple phases (canary -> ramp -> full). The prototype explores: a lane-based phase view with tokenized traffic markers, an emergency brake that pauses traffic at phase boundaries, inline health indicators driven by telemetry (latency/error %), and a lightweight rollback assistant that suggests next steps when signals cross thresholds. This ticket covers low-fidelity flows, one interactive prototype for testing with PMs/eng, and a review-ready spec for handoff to frontend engineering.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Phase lane canvas that shows at least three sequential phases with adjustable percentages and a clear active phase marker.
2) Emergency brake control that can pause progression and emit a contextual confirmation modal.
3) Inline health overlays (latency/error) visible per phase and driven by placeholder telemetry values.
4) Rollback assistant panel that surfaces suggested actions (snapback, isolate phase, route 0%) with links to runbooks.
5) Prototype linked in Figma and walkthrough recorded; PM and ENG feedback captured and triaged.
6) Implementation notes for dev: component list, accessibility considerations, and unit of work estimate attached.
design_notes: Core components: phase lane (compact horizontal segments), traffic tokens (draggable to reassign %), semaphore iconography (green/yellow/red states), emergency brake (sticky toggle + cooldown), scrubber timeline to preview phased timing, health sparkline per phase. Interactions: drag token -> live delta preview; click phase boundary -> open micro-settings (rollout window, metric guards); panic: emergency brake triggers two-step confirm and locks tokens; rollback assistant computes minimal delta to restore baseline and suggests canary rollback or full revert. Accessibility: keyboard reassign of tokens, ARIA labels for phase states, clear color contrast for semaphore states. Performance: expect minimal DOM nodes; suggest virtualization for >12 phases. Privacy/security: event of emergency brake action must be auditable (link to audit log event schema).
